headline: pki.smime.verify / decrypt can now recognize a legacy (RFC 8551) header-protected message -- opt in with `legacyHeaderProtection` and the real headers of an older `message/rfc822`-wrapped message are surfaced, safely separated from the authenticated header set.
summary: S/MIME header protection (RFC 9788) gains inbound support for the legacy RFC 8551 scheme (RFC 9788 sec. 4.10): a message whose signed/encrypted payload is a bare `message/rfc822` object carrying the real headers, with no `hp=` parameter. Pass `opts.legacyHeaderProtection: true` to `pki.smime.verify` or `pki.smime.decrypt` and a legacy message that meets the RFC 9788 sec. 4.10.1 identification test has its inner headers surfaced under `headerProtection.legacy` -- a `{ headers, mode, fromMismatch, confidential }` object whose `headers` is an ordered `[{ name, value }]` array that retains legally-repeated fields (a delivered message's multiple `Received` trace headers are all preserved), with the mode inferred from the envelope (`clear` for signed, `cipher` for encrypted) and, for an encrypted message, the confidential set derived from the actual visible outer headers. Because a legacy message is structurally indistinguishable from an ordinary forwarded `message/rfc822`, the inference is deliberately kept out of `protectedHeaders` and never sets `headerProtection.present`: those remain reserved for the cryptographically-declared (`hp=`) header set a caller may trust, so a consumer keying trust off `present`/`protectedHeaders` can never mistake the opt-in heuristic for authenticated headers. Consuming `headerProtection.legacy.headers` is an explicit choice and comes with `legacy.fromMismatch` to flag a forwarded message whose inner sender differs from the outer one. Detection is off by default and applies only after the signature/AEAD verdict succeeds; a nested crypto layer, an `hp=` on the inner message, a non-`message/rfc822` payload, or a duplicate Content-Type on either part reports `legacy: null`. No wire format changes; sending remains unchanged (RFC 9788 forbids generating the legacy wrap).

Added: pki.smime.verify and pki.smime.decrypt accept opts.legacyHeaderProtection: true to detect a legacy RFC 8551 header-protected message (RFC 9788 sec. 4.10) -- a signed or encrypted payload that is a bare message/rfc822 wrap with no hp= parameter. On a precise match the inner message's Non-Structural headers are surfaced under headerProtection.legacy = { headers, mode, fromMismatch, confidential }, with the mode inferred from the envelope and an encrypted message's confidential set computed against the visible outer headers. RFC 9788 sec. 4.10.1 / sec. 4.10.2, RFC 8551.

headerProtection.legacy is null on every verify / decrypt result unless a legacy message was detected via legacyHeaderProtection. The inferred set is intentionally kept separate from the authenticated protectedHeaders (which stays null) and from present (which stays false), since a legacy message is indistinguishable from a forwarded message/rfc822 -- so a consumer keying trust off present/protectedHeaders is never misled by the opt-in heuristic, and consuming headerProtection.legacy.headers is an explicit, fromMismatch-checkable choice.
Changed: Detection is opt-in and safe-by-default. Without legacyHeaderProtection the behavior is unchanged: a legacy-form message reads as protectedHeaders: null, present: false, legacy: null (never mis-authenticated). With the option set, a message that is not precisely identified -- an ordinary forwarded message/rfc822 that fails a condition, an inner part that is itself a signed/encrypted layer, an inner part declaring hp=, or a part with a duplicate Content-Type -- reports legacy: null. The signed-and-encrypted legacy form (RFC 9788 Appendix C.3.17) surfaces as clear via the caller's re-verify step, a documented limitation of the non-recursive layered API.
